title: Rabbi Yosi bar Huna
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Sanhedrin 105b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.105b) attributes to him the famous saying that Ruth was the daughter of Eglon, the grandson of Balak king of Moab. The reading should be Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Chanina, as the saying appears in [Nazir 23b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.23b) and [Horayot 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.10b). In [Sotah 47a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.47a) it is attributed to Rabbi Yosi ben Choni; that is also the reading of Dikdukei Soferim in Sanhedrin.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman’s proposed correction is retained as his textual judgment, not an independently verified genealogy or identification. ב״ב של means grandson of: Eglon, not Ruth, is the grandson in the reported saying. The three distinct attributions—bar Huna, son of Rabbi Chanina and ben Choni—are not merged. דק״ס is the customary Dikdukei Soferim. The printed קה:, כג:, י: and מז. conventionally give 105b, 23b, 10b and 47a; the complete matching Davidson Hebrew passages have now been checked; Dikdukei Soferim remains an attributed, unverified reading.

The native printed heading on volume II, p. 721 (PDF page 304), spells רבי יוסי בר הונא in full; an earlier provisional Rav heading is not adopted. Davidson’s Sanhedrin 105b:12 likewise explicitly names Rabbi Yosi bar Huna. Nazir 23b:10 and Horayot 10b:18 explicitly have Rabbi Yosi berabbi Chanina, supporting both title words in that attributed form. Sotah 47a:3 explicitly has Rabbi Yosi ben Choni. The genealogical details also differ: Nazir and Horayot call Ruth Eglon’s granddaughter, while Sanhedrin and Sotah call her his daughter; Sotah calls Eglon Balak’s son, while Sanhedrin calls him Balak’s grandson. Hyman’s own summary remains as printed, and the parallel attributions do not merge those people or prove his proposed correction.
